The evidence, and why it is paper only
Priced on futures, the contract you trade (futures lab, 23 Oct 2026): 2005–2020 +0.15% a trade, not reliable month to month (t 1.92); 2020–2026 +0.07% a trade (t −0.14). Share prices flatter a short by about 0.1% a trade, and every figure below is share-priced. Tested on NSE 2005–2020, data it had never seen, with its rules fixed first: 33,979 trades, +0.21% a trade after futures charges, t 4.66, positive in every 5-year period but shrinking (+0.40%, +0.31%, +0.14%); it lost −0.48% a trade in the 2020 COVID crash. Found on 2020–2026 (+0.30% then +0.13% a trade). Not yet checked with the full deflated Sharpe. On paper since 2026-10-05: 100 trades, +0.2% a trade, 50% winners — a verdict needs 100 trades and 3 months (about early January 2027). One trade is about +0.2% on average and can lose several percent on a rally day; it works only over many trades. Real money on Zerodha only after a PASS.

Most rows are in: Financial Services 10, Automobile and Auto Components 9, Information Technology 8. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend, a row's target comes before its stop at most as often as its break-even (about 37.5%) — a price with no trend is a fair game — so before GM's charges these rows make money only if the BUY signal works. It was tested and FAILED: the desk’s own rating, replayed day by day on six years of NSE’s own prices (2,36,746 stock-days), bought on this tab’s limit, target and stop, made −0.028% a trade after charges, 36.7% winners where 37.5% are needed (32,725 trades, t = −0.44).

Calls — you BUY the call, it pays if the stock RISES

NO TRADE — nothing on this tab has passed a test. So there is nothing here the desk can call a suggestion. Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The call rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 202 call rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹35,76,268 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹18,12,965 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 202 rows are on 32 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Information Technology 61, Financial Services 45, Automobile and Auto Components 17. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a call is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹31,933.22 across all 202 rows, one lot each, plus the bid-ask spread, which is not known without a live book (138 of these rows). 48 of 202 are priced above the stock’s own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the BUY signal works, and it failed: the desk’s own rating, replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, made −0.028% a trade on its BUY and ACCUMULATE rows (32,725 trades, 36.7% winners).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹8,99,428 or worse · worst day: −₹25,42,282 · market opens 5% lower: −₹23,81,411
Today’s 202 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 495 trading days, Wed, 30 Oct 2024 to Thu, 29 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 495 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹8,99,428 — ₹12,07,625 on average.
Worst day, Mon, 7 Apr 2025 (NIFTY −3.24%): 32 of 32 stocks fell and 201 stops were hit, 185 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹25,42,282, against −₹17,87,942 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% lower: −₹23,81,411. Each stock opens lower by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.09), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 93.1% of the stocks fell at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 32 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: COFORGE 8.4%, POLYCAB 5.8%, PNB 5.7%, ETERNAL 5.6%, UNIONBANK 5.4%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Thu, 29 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For calls these figures are the pessimistic end. Each call is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — and in a crash that volatility jumps, which cushions a call (India VIX moved +66% on Mon, 7 Apr 2025). Puts — you BUY the put, it pays if the index or stock FALLS

NO TRADE — nothing on this tab has passed a test. So there is nothing here the desk can call a suggestion. Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The put rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 48 put rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹8,32,554 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹4,28,284 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 48 rows are on 12 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Financial Services 17, Capital Goods 11, Power 6. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a put is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹15,333.36 across all 48 rows, one lot each, plus the bid-ask spread, which is not known without a live book (14 of these rows). 8 of 48 are priced above their own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the fall continues, and selling NIFTY in these downtrends failed its pre-registered test (final year t = 0.205).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹2,13,653 or worse · worst day: −₹4,87,364 · market opens 5% higher: −₹5,22,764
Today’s 48 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 495 trading days, Wed, 30 Oct 2024 to Thu, 29 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 495 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹2,13,653 — ₹2,81,593 on average.
Worst day, Tue, 3 Feb 2026 (NIFTY +2.55%): 12 of 12 names rose and 43 stops were hit, 30 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹4,87,364, against −₹4,16,521 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% higher: −₹5,22,764. Each name opens higher by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.25), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 94% of the names rose at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 12 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: BHEL 17.1%, ADANIPOWER 16.6%, CGPOWER 16.3%, INDUSINDBK 8.6%, LTF 8.2%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Thu, 29 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For puts these figures are the OPTIMISTIC end. Each put is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — but a put loses on the days the market rises, and on those days implied volatility usually falls, which takes still more off a put (India VIX moved −7% on Tue, 3 Feb 2026). The real loss on such a day can be larger than shown.
The stock puts lean on the desk’s SELL and REDUCE ratings, and those were tested: shorting them LOST. Replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, shorting every SELL/REDUCE row on this desk’s limit, target and stop made −0.139% a trade (35,236 trades, t = −3.31 — reliably negative), and over 20 sessions those stocks did slightly BETTER than the market. They are shown because you asked for the falling names, not because the rating picks fallers.
These options are priced from NSE’s 2026-10-28 settlement file, a session older than today’s last trades (2026-10-29). NSE publishes the 2026-10-29 file after about 19:00 IST, and the next build after that uses it. The futures tab already uses today’s last trades.

FORWARD PAPER TEST: SELLING NIFTY OPTIONS ON EXPIRY DAY · PASSED its test (351 expiries) · paper only
COLLECTING — X2, sell the ATM call and put at the open, buy a leg back at 2x: 1 expiries, +89.59 points an expiry (+₹5,823 a lot), 100% won, worst 89.59 points.
Worst expiry in the test: −3.19% of NIFTY — about −732 points, −₹48,000 a lot of 65 at NIFTY 22,936.75. Selling needs margin: about ₹2.6 lakh a lot on expiry day (Zerodha, 25 Oct).
Call side +15.0, put side +2.6 points an expiry in the test: no proven difference (t −1.48). One side alone is a bet on NIFTY’s direction.
Call against put (studies/expiry-legs-2026-10-25, rules fixed before the split was computed): a sold call loses when NIFTY rises, a sold put when it falls. On the 157 expiries NIFTY rose, the call side lost 27.3 points and the put side made 47.6; on the 194 it fell, the call side made 49.3 and the put side lost 33.9. Together they made money both ways (+20.3, +15.4). The put side’s stop was hit more often (42% of expiries against 31%), and it had the worst day (−287 points, 3 Feb 2026).
The study (2020–2026, NSE’s own files, after charges): +17.6 points an expiry for X2, t 4.43, positive in every period; its worst expiry lost 3.19% of NIFTY. Counted from 2026-10-27; a verdict after 52 expiries (CONFIRMED needs mean above 0 and t ≥ 1.68). Rules fixed in studies/expiry-selling-forward-2026-10-21/PREREGISTRATION.txt. Data through 2026-10-28. Selling options needs margin and can lose far more than the premium; this is information, never a row to trade.

Hit rate counts only trades that filled and then finished. IF RANDOM is how often the target would come before the stop if prices moved at random — each trade's break-even, before charges. Only a hit rate above it, over enough separate bets, is evidence of an edge. The touch odds the desk showed ignore the stop, so they always run higher. Futures returns are GROSS per unit; options are NET of every charge per lot. ALL has no average return (futures move about 1.5%, options about 50%), and its money is options net a lot plus futures at 20 units, gross.

HOW THIS IS SCORED. Every price this page freezes is bought on paper at the moment it is shown. Each build then checks the market, using the day’s high and low so a move between two builds is not missed. Every ambiguity counts against the record: a target and a stop in the same window is a stop; a target in the same window as the fill is not counted; a gap through the stop exits at the open; a fill is always at the limit, never better; a price from before the level was shown can never fill it. Unfilled day orders die at 15:30. Futures are held at most 20 sessions; options until expiry. Stored in the private repository under docs/ledger/, committed on every build, and copied to the Google Sheet.
WHERE THESE PRICES COME FROM. Option premiums are from NSE’s 2026-10-28 settlement file (NSE posts the 2026-10-29 file after about 19:00 IST; the next build uses it); futures NOW is the 2026-10-29 last trade. The market was closed when this was built, so nothing here is executable right now. Premiums and the futures prices they are measured against both come from that same settlement file, so they describe the same moment. Checked against NSE's own site at 2026-10-29 16:24 IST: 16 of 16 sampled contracts are the same contract on both (the same previous close), last prices identical. Broker login OK from the build server at 2026-10-29 16:23 IST — a NIFTY quote came back. F&O ban for 2026-10-29: KAYNES, SAIL — left out entirely, because NSE allows only exits in a banned stock. This page is a snapshot, rebuilt on a schedule — it is not a live feed. Check the price on your broker before placing anything. Net figures are after brokerage, STT at 0.15%, exchange, stamp and GST; the spread is extra and is only known where a live book was seen.
NO SHOCK SHIELD. Nothing on this page stops buys on a bad global morning — not a GIFT Nifty gap, a crude or S&P move, or an India VIX spike. Those signals were tested on NSE’s own data and failed (or had too few events to test), so they do not gate anything. Check the market yourself before acting on a shock day.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That any of it makes money. The paper ledger so far: futures 53 targets and 261 stops, 16.2% hit (95% range 9.3–23.2%); short futures 78 targets and 100 stops, 43.3% hit (95% range 25.3–61.4%); calls 444 targets and 1206 stops, 26% hit (95% range 18–34.1%); puts 1557 targets and 1272 stops, 54% hit (95% range 42.6–65.4%), over only 24 sessions of the same market. That says how this market went, not that a rule works — each row shows its own break-even. And every test fixed in advance so far, on data never used to build the rule, found no edge: the desk's own rating (replayed on six years of NSE data: −0.03% a trade on its buys, and its SELL/REDUCE shorts LOST −0.14% a trade, t = −3.3), 12-1 momentum, time-series momentum, low volatility, a 10-month market trend filter, and the NIFTY trend reader that now chooses between buys and puts (selling NIFTY in its downtrends: final year t = 0.21) — all six FAIL. The ranking is built on things that were measured, which is not the same as an edge that was proven. Size accordingly.
